newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone H1 rises, buys Peoples Phone.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone H1 rises, buys Peoples Phone.

text.p: Britain's largest mobile telephone company Vodafone Plc reported a sharp rise in pretax profits for the first half of 1996 on Thursday, helped by debut international income gains, and said it would buy local UK company Peoples Phone.

A 21 percent rise in its pretax profit to 252.4 million pounds ($422.8 million) was boosted by an additional 11.1 million pound gain from the sale of fixed assets, and the company raised its interim dividend by 20 percent to 2.36 pence.

"The group has maintained its excellent growth record, with continued progress from both the established business in the United Kingdom and its overseas operations," the company said in a statement. It now has over 3.5 million subscribers.
Vodafone said its overseas operations passed through break even in August "and are now contributing to the group's operating profit."
"In many of the group's overseas markets, cellular penetration is low and substantial growth is projected. Profits from the group's international operations should therefore continue to increase."

Explaining its move to buy Peoples Phone Co Plc, its biggest single UK service provider, for a total of some 77 million pounds, Vodafone said the deal would add 395,500 subcribers as well as its chain of 181 retail outlets.
